title: Impact of Microfinance Branch Entry on Household Consumption

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with unit (household) and period fixed effects (TWFE).
- Why: We observe households in treated and control regions before and after microfinance branch entry, with an interaction term treat_x_post = treated × post. TWFE DID differences out time-invariant household heterogeneity and common time shocks, identifying the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) under parallel trends.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: Absent branch entry, treated and control households’ log consumption would have followed parallel paths.
  - No spillovers: Treatment in a region does not affect control households.
  - No anticipatory effects: Households do not change consumption before entry in anticipation.
  - Stable composition and consistent measurement over time.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load or install required packages
req_pkgs <- c("data.table", "fixest", "dplyr")
inst <- req_pkgs[!sapply(req_pkgs, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(inst) > 0) install.packages(inst, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(dplyr)

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s39_data.csv"
df <- fread(path)

# Basic checks and cleaning
if (!all(c("unit_id","period","treated","post","treat_x_post","y") %in% names(df))) {
  stop("Expected columns are missing from the dataset.")
}
# Ensure types are appropriate
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    unit_id = as.integer(unit_id),
    period = as.integer(period),
    treated = as.integer(treated),
    post = as.integer(post),
    treat_x_post = as.integer(treat_x_post),
    y = as.numeric(y)
  )

# Drop missing observations if any
df <- df %>% filter(is.finite(y), !is.na(treat_x_post), !is.na(unit_id), !is.na(period))

# 2) Descriptive: group means by treatment and period
desc <- df %>%
  group_by(treated, post) %>%
  summarise(mean_log_cons = mean(y), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
cat("Group means (log consumption) by treated x post:\n")
print(desc)

# 3) Main DID: TWFE with two-way clustering (unit and period)
m_twfe <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df, cluster = ~ unit_id + period)
summ_twfe <- summary(m_twfe)

# Extract main effect and CI
b <- coef(m_twfe)["treat_x_post"]
se <- sqrt(vcov(m_twfe)["treat_x_post","treat_x_post"])
ci <- confint(m_twfe, "treat_x_post", level = 0.95)
att_pct <- (exp(b) - 1) * 100

cat("\nMAIN RESULT (TWFE DID with two-way clustering):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef on treat_x_post (log points): %.4f\n", b))
cat(sprintf("  SE: %.4f | 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", se, ci[1], ci[2]))
cat(sprintf("  Interpretation: %.2f%% change in consumption\n", att_pct))

# 4) Robustness A: Simple DID (no unit FE), cluster by unit_id
m_simple <- feols(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df, cluster = ~ unit_id)
b_s <- coef(m_simple)["treat_x_post"]
se_s <- sqrt(vcov(m_simple)["treat_x_post","treat_x_post"])
ci_s <- confint(m_simple, "treat_x_post", level = 0.95)
att_pct_s <- (exp(b_s) - 1) * 100

cat("\nROBUSTNESS A (Simple DID with cluster by unit_id):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef on treat_x_post (log points): %.4f\n", b_s))
cat(sprintf("  SE: %.4f | 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", se_s, ci_s[1], ci_s[2]))
cat(sprintf("  Interpretation: %.2f%% change in consumption\n", att_pct_s))

# 5) Robustness B: Pre-trend test in pre-periods only (needs >= 2 distinct pre periods)
pre_df <- df %>% filter(post == 0)
pre_periods <- sort(unique(pre_df$period))
if (length(pre_periods) >= 2) {
  # Differential trend: y_it = alpha_i + gamma_t + beta * (treated_i * period_t) + e_it
  m_pretrend <- feols(y ~ treated:period | unit_id + period, data = pre_df, cluster = ~ unit_id + period)
  # Identify coefficient name robustly
  cname <- names(coef(m_pretrend))[grepl("^treated[:*]period$", names(coef(m_pretrend)))]
  if (length(cname) == 0) cname <- names(coef(m_pretrend))[1]
  b_pt <- coef(m_pretrend)[cname]
  se_pt <- sqrt(vcov(m_pretrend)[cname, cname])
  z_pt <- b_pt / se_pt
  p_pt <- 2 * pnorm(abs(z_pt), lower.tail = FALSE)
  cat("\nROBUSTNESS B (Pre-trend test in pre-periods):\n")
  cat(sprintf("  Coef on treated:period (diff. trend): %.4f | SE: %.4f | p-value: %.4f\n", b_pt, se_pt, p_pt))
  if (is.finite(p_pt) && p_pt > 0.10) {
    cat("  Result: No evidence of differential pre-trends (fail to reject H0 at 10%).\n")
  } else {
    cat("  Warning: Potential differential pre-trends (reject H0 at 10%).\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("\nROBUSTNESS B (Pre-trend test): Not enough pre-periods to test pre-trends.\n")
}

# 6) Robustness C: Alternative clustering (unit-only)
m_twfe_uc <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df, cluster = ~ unit_id)
b_uc <- coef(m_twfe_uc)["treat_x_post"]
se_uc <- sqrt(vcov(m_twfe_uc)["treat_x_post","treat_x_post"])
ci_uc <- confint(m_twfe_uc, "treat_x_post", level = 0.95)
att_pct_uc <- (exp(b_uc) - 1) * 100
cat("\nROBUSTNESS C (TWFE with unit-only clustering):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef on treat_x_post (log points): %.4f\n", b_uc))
cat(sprintf("  SE: %.4f | 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", se_uc, ci_uc[1], ci_uc[2]))
cat(sprintf("  Interpretation: %.2f%% change in consumption\n", att_pct_uc))

# Final clear numerical result
cat("\nFINAL NUMERICAL RESULT (Preferred TWFE DID):\n")
cat(sprintf("  ATT on log consumption = %.4f (SE = %.4f), 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n", b, se, ci[1], ci[2]))
cat(sprintf("  Implied percent change in consumption = %.2f%%\n", att_pct))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Microfinance access should modestly relax liquidity constraints and smooth consumption.
- Magnitude: Small to moderate. I expect an ATT of about 0.03–0.08 log points (≈3%–8%) on household consumption. Effects are often modest in the short run, reflecting limited take-up and substitution toward business investment, but a small positive consumption response is plausible.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in household consumption before and after microfinance branch entry between treated and untreated regions.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The entry of a microfinance branch is associated with a positive effect on household consumption.
_ground_truth.main_effect: Approximately 0.15 increase in log household consumption.
